author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Bangladesh is battling what the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention lists as the world’s largest current measles outbreak, with 999 suspected and confirmed measles-related deaths reported since March, Reuters reported Wednesday.

Authorities have recorded more than 166,000 suspected cases. Of those, 19,835 were laboratory confirmed, while more than 146,000 people were hospitalized. The outbreak has spread as routine immunization was disrupted during 2024 and 2025 and vaccine shortages left gaps in protection.

An emergency measles-rubella campaign has reached more than 19.7 million children. Health specialists say catch-up vaccination and restoration of routine immunization remain essential because a one-time campaign cannot fully repair missed doses or stop continued transmission.

Hospitals are also managing dengue cases, adding pressure to staff and beds. The death and case counts can change as records are reviewed, but the scale already shows how quickly measles can spread when vaccination coverage falls. Measles is highly contagious, and outbreaks can become especially dangerous for young children and people with limited access to care.
dek: Authorities have recorded more than 166,000 suspected cases as disrupted immunization and vaccine shortages fuel a fast-moving public-health emergency.
headline: Bangladesh measles outbreak nears 1,000 deaths
